The six terminal completion cases fail their persisted round-trip assertion. SQL commits
the compound accounting, but the loaded StrategyResultReceipt loses ExecutionRunId.

Root cause: ProcessPersistenceMappers.SerializeDiagnostics writes the legacy array
when HostCapabilityEvidence is null. ExecutionRunId is stored on each diagnostic entry.
An empty diagnostic array therefore cannot retain the supplied execution identity.
This is not an attestation requirement: ResolvePersistedExecutionRunId permits no
attestation and rejects contradictory supplied attestations. Preserve that rule.

Minimal correction, after reconciling and retaining the frozen run:

- Keep the exact legacy array for no host evidence when execution identity is absent
  or at least one diagnostic carries it.
- For an empty diagnostic list with an execution identity, write the existing version-1
  object, which already has ResultExecutionRunId and nullable HostCapabilityEvidence.
- Preserve the decoder and all identity/attestation consistency checks. No schema or
  database migration, receipt version, inferred attestation or authorization change.
- Run the existing result acceptance guard against the persisted state already loaded
  by the unit of work before returning, still inside its fenced transaction. This adds
  no query and prevents a future mapper or storage discrepancy from committing a
  terminal result whose original execution identity was lost.
- Add independent mapper tests for empty diagnostics and null host evidence, original
  array compatibility, exact execution lookup, and malformed/conflicting identity.
- Inject loss of the serialized identity after SaveChanges and require complete
  rollback of runtime, result, child and budget in the real PostgreSQL transaction.
- Repeat the complete affected candidate and existing ProcessPersistenceStoreTests;
  direct-build Persistence and refresh standard Unit/Integration outputs. Repeat full
  static enforcement and the architecture diff for the changed mapper.
